title: Parity Anomaly as Modular Commutator with Massless Dirac Fermion
abstract: The modular commutator $J(A,B,C) = i\langle[K_{AB},K_{BC}]\rangle$ extracts the chiral central charge $c_-$ from a single bulk wavefunction of a \emph{gapped} 2d state, where $3J/π=c_-$. Inspired by the recent developments in the field of gapless symmetry-protected topological phases, we ask: what does the modular commutator measure, if it is well-defined at all, when the 2d bulk becomes \textit{gapless}? Several interesting new insights can already be obtained using the simple Haldane honeycomb model. For the critical point hosting an isolated Dirac node we find that $J$ remains sharp: it converges to a \textit{half-quantized} value, with corrections that decay as a power law in the subsystem size rather than exponentially, mirroring the power-law correlations in gapless systems. We prove the half-quantization using an emergent reflection symmetry of the massless Dirac cone, and show that the half-quantized contribution comes from the other gapped cone (the massive partner of the massless one). This massive partner can be interpreted as the physical incarnation of the Pauli-Villars regulator, which is the origin of the parity-breaking level-$\frac{1}{2}$ Chern-Simons term (with half-quantized Hall conductance) and the parity anomaly. When protected chiral edge modes coexist with a bulk Dirac node we obtain $3J/π= c_-+\frac{1}{2}$. The half-quantization is also shown to be robust against tripartition deformation, tuning Dirac velocity and Dirac cone anisotropy. We further investigate other types of gaplessness---quadratic nodes (in contrast to linear Dirac) and the case with Fermi surface---and show that the robust half-quantization of $J$ is lost in such non-Dirac cases. These results generalize the modular commutator beyond gapped phases, and at the same time provide an information-theoretic measurement of the parity anomaly.
summary: This work extends the concept of the modular commutator, originally used to measure the chiral central charge in gapped topological phases, to gapless systems. The key finding is that at a Dirac node, the commutator yields a robust half-quantized value, which the authors interpret as the entanglement signature of the parity anomaly. This provides a novel, information-theoretic measurement tool for topological properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates what the modular commutator measures when the 2D bulk state transitions from a gapped phase to a gapless phase, generalizing its utility beyond gapped systems.
main_result: For a single Dirac node, the modular commutator exhibits a robust half-quantized value, which is proposed to be the entanglement manifestation of the parity anomaly. This quantization is lost in other types of gaplessness like Fermi surfaces.
method: The analysis uses the modular commutator $J(A,B,C)$ formalism, comparing its behavior in gapped versus gapless regimes, and employing symmetry arguments and correlation function analysis.
model_or_system: The primary model is the free-fermion Haldane honeycomb model, studied at its critical point hosting an isolated Dirac node. The analysis also considers systems with chiral edge modes and compares results to quadratic nodes and Fermi surfaces.
key_observables: Modular Commutator ($J$), Chiral Central Charge ($c^-$), Half-quantized value (1/2), Hall conductance ($\sigma_{xy}$), and Conditional Mutual Information ($	ext{CMI}$).
important_parameters: Dirac velocity, Dirac cone anisotropy, system size (for finite-size corrections), and energy cutoff ($\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the free-fermion approximation and assumes that the half-quantization is robust against tripartition deformation for the Dirac node case.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup using the Haldane model, showing the MC converging to 0.5 at the critical point, and comparing entanglement scaling for different gapless systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the gapped case where $J$ measures $c^-$, to the gapless Dirac node case where $J$ is half-quantized, and finally generalizes the analysis by comparing this behavior to other gapless scenarios and relating it to the parity anomaly.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between entanglement measures (modular commutator) and fundamental topological invariants (parity anomaly, Chern number) provides a powerful, information-theoretic tool for characterizing topological phases, which is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory.
